text: I notice you are a pediatric patient presenting with systemic hypertension. To begin our assessment, how old are you, and have you noticed any symptoms like headaches, blurred vision, or decreased exercise tolerance?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Since this was a routine visit, may I ask if his blood pressure was elevated on multiple readings, and have you noticed any episodes of snoring or restless sleep?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is unusual, as hypertension should be systemic rather than isolated to one arm. Can you confirm if his blood pressure is also elevated in the left arm, or is it normal there?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Born full term with an uneventful neonatal period. Social history: Patient attends kindergarten. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco smoke.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is his blood pressure elevated in the lower extremities as well, or is it significantly lower than in his right arm? I need to determine if this is isolated upper extremity hypertension or a discrepancy suggestive of a vascular obstruction.

speaker: Patient
text: All systems review is essentially negative as reported by the mother.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify the blood pressure discrepancy; is his blood pressure significantly lower in his lower extremities compared to his right arm? REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Echocardiogram findings show narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation. Left ventricular function is normal.

speaker: Doctor
text: The echocardiogram confirms coarctation of the aorta, which explains the blood pressure discrepancy. DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta
